title: Need for Grace
definition: The need for grace is the truth that fallen sinners cannot save, cleanse, or renew themselves and must be rescued by God's undeserved mercy in Christ.
summary: Humanity needs grace because sin has made self-salvation impossible.
christFocus: Jesus is the gift of grace, sent by God to save those who could never save themselves.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Humanity's need for grace flows from the reality of sin. People are not spiritually neutral or able to earn rescue through effort. Sin brings guilt, corruption, bondage, and separation from God.

Grace is God's undeserved favor toward the undeserving. It is not God rewarding the worthy, but God saving sinners through Christ.

The need for grace humbles pride and gives hope to the broken. If salvation depended on human worthiness, no one could stand. But grace opens the door to forgiveness, renewal, adoption, and life.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people either try to prove they are good enough or believe they are too broken to be helped. The need for grace matters because it tells the proud to stop boasting and the ashamed to stop despairing.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Admit your need before God. Receive grace through Christ, and extend grace to others as one who has been shown mercy. Let grace lead you to humility and holiness.
